label: Fix memory-server test failures — B3 curate handler + tool count
summary: Fixed 11/12 memory-server test failures: 2 backend.spec.ts tool count assertions (19→20 for WP-3 memory_write_batch) and 9 memory-tools.spec.ts curate failures caused by a missing `await` before async memoryCurate() in the WriteQueue callback.

changes.kind: Updated tool count expectations from 19 to 20 (WP-3 added memory_write_batch)
Added `async` to WriteQueue callback + `await` before memoryCurate() call in memory_curate handler

tests.output_snippet: 83 passed, 1 failed (pre-existing flake timeout in permission-guard.spec.ts)

issues: Pre-existing flaky test: permission-guard.spec.ts 'long content auto-chunks into parent + chunks with DERIVED_FROM edges' times out at 5005ms (just over the 5000ms limit). Per spec: do NOT fix.
handoff_notes: ROOT CAUSE: memoryCurate() in libs/memory-core/src/curate.ts is declared `async` (returns Promise<CurateResult>), but the WriteQueue callback in index.ts's memory_curate case was synchronous. The callback received a Promise object, not the actual result. 'code' in Promise → false (Promises have no enumerable `code` property), so the error branch was skipped. JSON.stringify(Promise<...>) → '{}' because Promises have no enumerable own properties.
Fix: made the callback `async` and added `await` before memoryCurate(writeDb, args). This pattern already exists in memory_write and memory_update handlers.

The other 3 operators using WriteQueue (memory_write, memory_invalidate, memory_link, memory_update) were correct — either their callbacks were already async+await, or the core function being called was synchronous.
backlog_entries: permission-guard.spec.ts: 'long content auto-chunks' flaky timeout (5005ms > 5000ms default). Needs longer timeout or optimization.
